I've been a huge fan of racing games ever since I was a kid, and I can honestly say this is my favorite Forza Horizon game so far. Waiting all these years was absolutely worth it.
The graphics are stunning, the driving feels fantastic and having the festival set in Japan makes the whole experience even better. I've always been interested in Japan so exploring the roads, cities and mountain passes is something I never get tired of. The map is beautiful and every drive feels like an adventure.
The car selection, customization, sound design and overall atmosphere are excellent. Whether you're cruising, drifting or racing. The game is just fun from start to finish.
My only small suggestion would be to add more NPCs especially in the city areas. Seeing more pedestrians and a busier world would make the environment feel even more alive and realistic.
Overall Playground Games absolutely delivered. If you're a fan of open-world racing games, this is an easy recommendation. Definitely my favorite Horizon game.

ABSOLUTE CINEMA! This game is such a huge jump from FH5, and is now my favorite game of all time. I was truly blown away by the exquisite attention to detail and beautiful graphics of the game, even at low-medium graphics settings. Half the time I get a view of Mt. Fuji, I have to get a picture of it with my car. My only complaint is that there should be a tutorial or at least some better instructions on how to use the camera, especially on keyboard. I had kind of a hard time figuring out how to position the camera to my liking at first, but I eventually got it. 9.8/10!

Best Horizon game, not many strings attached, Japan is simply the perfect festival location and it shows. Last game had plenty of stuttering issues whereas this one runs like butter while looking amazing. It's the best racing game on the market but I still think there's a lot of room for improvements. AI straight up cheats at higher levels of difficulty and while it's fun to look at all the bowieknife99 memes it's less funny when you have to redo a race because you got passed on the straight by a Saturn V missile. Progression is also a big no no, at least for me, the game floods you with cars but this is just how Horizon games works so I can't really complain. Houses are still a missed opportunity, Test Drive Unlimited did it better 20 years ago. With that said, I literally devoured this game in the few days since the release, it's fun, nothing else really matters.

The good:
- Pretty graphics
- Fun music

The bad:

- Really bad UI. Maybe it's considered passable on a console, but it's awful on a PC.
- The lead voiceover (Mei) was so grating that I had to mute dialogue to make the game tolerable.
- Crashy - it's silently crashed twice for me
- Audio is unstable - it just started cutting out sporadically as I was playing
- Absurdly large - why is a racing game over 150 GB?
- Some of the game physics is... questionable
Great game! I spent most of my time knocking out the side quests and modifying cars. The main storyline was good and the AI was very tough to beat in some races.

The game feels a bit undercooked. It's well optimized, runs smoothly on my PC, and I haven't hit any bugs. The graphics are pretty decent. However, the map feels empty and offers a lot less variety than I'd hoped.

My main complaint: the vast majority of vehicles are left-hand drive, which totally breaks immersion and feels disorienting as someone who lives in a country that drives on the left, playing a game set in a country that also drives on the left. It feels like pure laziness — a corner cut for no good reason — and it's put me off driving about 90% of the vehicles in the game.
